case_for: Campus ambassador network is a cheap, on-the-ground channel to a reachable segment (R2, R4).
Parent co-signer data is a plausible underwriting angle for thin-file borrowers (R6).
Pre-seed round the fund could lead (S2).
case_against: Default risk and licence sit with an NBFC partner: the defining risk appears delegated (R1).
No repayment or default data at all (R3 missing).
Hard collections from students and regulatory scrutiny of digital lending (R4).
Crowded BNPL category; fintech by label more than substance (S4, G3).
call_questions: When a student defaults, whose money is lost and how much first-loss do you carry?
What are your repayment and default numbers by cohort so far, and how do co-signed loans compare?
How do you collect from a student who has stopped responding, step by step?
If the RBI tightened digital-lending rules again tomorrow, what changes in your model?
Our biggest worry is that the NBFC holds the risk and you hold the growth target: convince us otherwise.
what_would_change_our_view: Cohort repayment data and evidence that the company holds and manages credit risk itself (first-loss, own collections) would change our view.
